extracted.intended_audience: early-career faculty (and their nominators) at invited US institutions considering Packard Fellowship nominations
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility requirements and scope for the David and Lucile Packard Foundation Fellowships, describing who may be nominated and what research disciplines and topics are eligible or excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty appointment at an invited institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be faculty members at one of the 50 Invited Institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page provides a full list of the 50 invited institutions (e.g., Brown, Caltech, Carnegie Mellon, Harvard, MIT, Stanford, Yale, etc.). Only faculty at these named institutions are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to serve as principal investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be eligible to serve as principal investigators engaged in research in the natural and physical sciences or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement that the candidate hold a faculty/PI-eligible position and lead independent research projects in eligible fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-career timing (within first three years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be within the first three years of their faculty careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict temporal eligibility window emphasizing support for researchers at the very start of their faculty appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplines considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplines that will be considered include physics, chemistry, mathematics, biology, astronomy, computer science, earth science, ocean science, and all branches of engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation explicitly lists the scientific and engineering fields that are in scope; use this list to determine disciplinary fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of social sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates engaged in research in the social sciences will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social science research is explicitly out of scope for the Packard Fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: "What We Don’t Fund" — areas with relatively generous funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Packard Fellowships do not fund certain areas of contemporary science and engineering that already have access to relatively generous funding (examples given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of areas generally not funded include clinical research; research associated with the design and construction of large national facilities such as accelerators and space stations; and applied research of direct relevance to national security. The program is directed to other, less supported fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference against well-established, well-funded faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship Program provides support for highly creative researchers early in their careers; faculty members who are well-established and well‐funded are less likely to receive the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program favors early-career investigators who need seed support for creative research directions rather than already well-funded, established investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to Fellowship Guidelines for details
rubrics_metrics.description: Please see the Fellowship Guidelines for detailed information about the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page points applicants to the Fellowship Guidelines for more complete rules, procedures, and any additional eligibility or application details not summarized on the eligibility page.
